title: Lightning Arrow Guide — Bow Lightning Chain, AoE Burst and Chaining
summary: Lightning Arrow is a bow attack gem: the arrow deals lightning damage and, on hit, arcs lightning chains to nearby enemies for a small AoE lightning burst. This guide explains how its chain picks targets, why it 'looks like it only hits one spot', how it interacts with Greater Multiple Projectiles / Chain / Fork, what Quality actually does, and why it is often used as a single-target burst alternative inside an Ice Shot build.
description: Lightning Arrow deep guide: chain target selection and range, comparison with Ice Shot / Lightning Rod / Lightning Warp, chain and damage supports, its role in Deadeye and Ice Shot builds, low-damage / no-chain causes with direct answers, video timestamps and real community questions.
author: Exile2 Guides Editorial

sections.title: Overview: One Arrow, a Whole Web of Lightning
paragraphs: Lightning Arrow is a bow attack gem: you fire an arrow that deals lightning damage, and on hit it arcs lightning chains from the impact point to nearby enemies, turning one shot into a small AoE lightning burst. It is neither a pure single-target arrow nor a pure projectile AoE — it is a hybrid of 'projectile hit + area chain'.

Its most misunderstood aspect is visual: the arrow itself appears to hit only one enemy, but a large share of the damage comes from the chains that arc out after the hit. If you only watch the arrow landing, it looks like overkill in dense packs yet 'does nothing' on a single boss — when in fact its value sits between the two: reliable output on the chosen target plus free splash ontonearby trash.

This is exactly why it is often slotted as a secondary burst inside Frost builds (Ice Shot Deadeye, etc.): Ice Shot handles chilling and clearing, while Lightning Arrow steps in when you need dependable single-target and chain filler damage. They share the bow and attack-speed system, so swapping costs almost nothing.
bullets: Essence: bow projectile + post-hit area lightning chain, hybrid single/AoE.
Damage sources: the arrow's own lightning damage + chains arcing from the hit.
Visual trap: arrow hits one, but the chains are the AoE body.
Common partner: Ice Shot Deadeye, as a single-target / chain-filler secondary.

sections.title: Mechanics: How the Chain Picks Targets
paragraphs: Chain trigger: when the arrow hits a primary target, it searches nearby enemies around the impact point and arcs lightning chains to them. The chain itself also deals damage, so one hit actually produces 'primary arrow lightning + surrounding chain lightning' as two outputs.

Target selection and range: the chain only looks for targets within a radius of the impact point, and usually deals chain damage to each chained enemy only once (no infinite ping-pong). This means the denser and tighter the pack, the more targets the chain reaches and the higher the overall payoff; spread-out singles or ranged enemies don't fill it.

The 'first hop' comes from the arrow hitting, so projectile hit rate directly decides whether the chain happens. If you use Greater Multiple Projectiles to fire several arrows, each arrow independently triggers its own chains on hit — that is the core trick that turns Lightning Arrow into a clear machine via multi-projectile, but it also means each arrow's single-target damage is split.
bullets: Chain arcs from the hit point to nearby enemies, dealing extra lightning.
Chain payoff scales with enemies near the impact; dense packs best.
Multi-projectile makes each arrow trigger its own chain — clear up, ST down.
Projectile hit rate is the prerequisite for the chain to occur.

Usually pick Chain or Fork, not both, to avoid logic conflicts.

sections.title: Role in Builds
paragraphs: Secondary burst in Ice Shot Deadeye: the primary Ice Shot handles chilling and clearing; when you hit something that can't be frozen or need reliable single-target, switch to Lightning Arrow — it outputs steadily without relying on ailments, acting as 'insurance when ailments fail'.

Pure Lightning Arrow clear build: use Greater Multiple Projectiles + Chain to turn Lightning Arrow itself into a clear machine, feeding chains off dense packs. Cost: weak single-target, needing a separate real boss skill.

Synergy with Herald of Ice / Thunder: elemental bow builds often run a Herald for extra elemental burst; Lightning Arrow's lightning pairs with Herald of Thunder's bolts for stacked clearing, but that adds Mana and Spirit load that must be balanced.
bullets: Ice Shot Deadeye: Lightning Arrow as ST insurance when ailments fail.
Clear build: multi-proj + Chain fills chains, but ST gets soft.
Pair with Herald for elemental stacking, watch Mana / Spirit budget.

sections.title: Common Mistakes: Low Damage / No Chains
paragraphs: Feels weak: you only watched the arrow landing and ignored the chains arcing to nearby enemies after the hit. Direct answer: test in dense packs — the chain payoff far exceeds the single arrow; on a lone boss it simply isn't its strongest form.

Chains don't appear: usually there is no second enemy near the impact (chains need nearby targets to arc), or the projectile missed entirely. Direct answer: confirm the arrow hit and that other enemies are near the target; solo targets naturally starve the chain.

Softer after multi-proj: Greater Multiple Projectiles splits damage across arrows, weakening each arrow's single-target. Direct answer: drop multi-proj for single-target bosses, reinstall for clearing.

Confusing Chain support with built-in chain: Chain support makes the projectile keep bouncing, while the built-in effect is the post-hit lightning chain — stacking both makes people think it 'double triggers'. Direct answer: understand they are independent and choose deliberately, not blindly stack.
bullets: Issue: low damage / no sense of AoE.
Direct answer: chains are the AoE body — verify in dense packs.
Direct answer: need a second enemy near the hit, and the arrow must connect.
Direct answer: drop multi-proj for ST, reinstall for clear.

items.question: How many times does the chain bounce?
answer: On hit it arcs a one-time chain to several nearby enemies; exact target count and range are per current client.
Chain payoff depends on enemies near the impact; dense packs benefit most.

items.question: What is the relation between Chain support and the built-in chain?
answer: Chain support makes the projectile itself keep bouncing after the primary target — a separate system from the built-in post-hit lightning chain.
They trigger independently; stacking too many muddies coverage logic, so choose deliberately.

items.question: Why does it get soft on bosses after multi-proj?
answer: Greater Multiple Projectiles splits total damage across arrows, weakening each arrow's single-target.
Drop multi-proj or switch to single-arrow for bosses, reinstall for clearing.
